items.title: Decision-making by proxy: A contextual study of data intermediaries
items.abstract: Ensuring privacy in digital ecosystems presents significant challenges. Individual privacy-related decision-making has been widely criticised as insufficient. The mobility context, where computing is typically ubiquitous, makes this type of decision-making also operationally infeasible. This study examines whether innovative data governance strategies offer a promising approach. Drawing on contextual integrity theory, this paper examines the perceived appropriateness of delegating privacy-related decision-making to different types of data intermediaries (data cooperatives, AI agents, and experts) in mobility contexts. Specifically, a stratified, full-factorial vignette study ( N = 600) is conducted. The vignettes systematically varied across four contextual factors: sender, information type, purpose, and duration of data access approval. This design allows for the examination of how contextual factors influence preferences for data intermediary-based decision-making in mobility settings. Findings show that scenarios in which data cooperatives acted as the decision-makers were consistently rated as more appropriate than those involving AI agents or experts, particularly in high-stakes contexts such as traffic management and ambulance coordination. Nevertheless, scenarios involving individual control received the highest overall appropriateness ratings. Respondents’ preferences were context-dependent: they showed greater acceptance when the purpose of sharing aligned with public benefit, and when the access duration was either short (e.g., one day) or revocable (e.g., ‘until revoked’). The results underscore the relevance of hybrid governance models that combine individual control with the ability to delegate decision-making to trusted intermediaries, particularly in mobility contexts. Together, these contributions could aid in developing context-sensitive privacy frameworks that align with societal values in ubiquitous computing environments.

items.title: Deconstruction and Interpretation of Advertising Cost‐Conversion Efficiency: Microlevel Feature Analysis Based on Machine Learning and SHAP
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Precisely deconstructing the numerical composition of advertising cost‐conversion efficiency (ACTE) and uncovering its microlevel associative mechanisms are critical for enterprises to optimize marketing decisions. To overcome the limitations of existing methods regarding modeling accuracy and result interpretability, this study constructs an analytical framework integrating machine learning with interpretable artificial intelligence. Using 174,584 real‐world microlevel advertising records from a Chinese telecommunications company in July 2024, we systematically compared six representative machine learning models, rigorously evaluating them against a historical average baseline. The findings reveal that the XGBoost model achieves optimal fitting and generalization performance, with a test set coefficient of determination of 0.8236 ± 0.2061, significantly outperforming the baseline and other models. Furthermore, SHAP‐based interpretability analysis not only precisely quantifies the contribution of each feature to the ACTE value but also systematically reveals underlying nonlinear dependencies and threshold effects. Specifically, the advertising conversion rate plays a dominant role; exposure frequency shows a step‐like positive association; production cost exhibits a reversal effect demarcated by the median; click‐through rate and play volume display discrete stratified structures; and average display cost contributes minimally. Specification tests indicate that ACTE interpretability primarily stems from algebraic relationships of constitutive features, with limited independent contributions from non‐constitutive features. Theoretically, this study provides microlevel evidence for nonlinear advertising associations; methodologically, it establishes a rigorous modeling‐to‐interpretation paradigm; and practically, it offers empirically grounded decision support for advertising exposure regulation and cost optimization.

items.title: Deep Learning and Graph Neural Networks for Drug-Like Molecule Modeling
items.abstract: The recent developments in artificial intelligence have had a significant influence on drug discovery, with the possibility of modeling drug-like molecules based on data. Graph neural networks and other deep learning methods have been shown to be effective for learning useful molecular representations, as well as for learning complex chemical structures directly based on data. The chapter offers an introduction to deep learning analysis through the focus on graph-based algorithms of the prediction of molecular properties, drug-likeness, and de novo generation of molecules. It talks about prominent molecular representations like SMILES, molecular fingerprints, and molecular graphs, and how they are incorporated into the current neural network models. The chapter also examines evaluation metrics and reports real-world research on the usefulness of these models in practical drug discovery. Lastly, it outlines the existing constraints, research gaps, and challenges in the future, insisting on the increased use of deep learning and GNNs in pharmaceutical discovery speeds and improvements.

items.title: Deep learning-based mitotic quantification for objective adjunct for grading of urothelial carcinoma: a multi-institutional validation study
items.abstract: Abstract Histological grading of urothelial carcinoma is subject to interobserver variability. We evaluated whether artificial intelligence (AI)-based whole-slide mitotic quantification provides an objective adjunct to histological grading. We developed and validated a deep learning-based mitotic detection framework trained on 91,183 patches with 318,893 annotations. A multi-reader crossover study was conducted in internal ( n = 149) and external ( n = 316) cohorts, where three independent pathologists graded cases in unassisted and model-assisted phases. In the combined cohort ( n = 465), AI-derived mitotic count showed high diagnostic accuracy for high-grade carcinoma (area under the curve [AUC] 0.91, 95% CI 0.89–0.94) at a cut-off of 17.5 mitoses per 2 mm². AI assistance significantly improved mean reader AUC from 0.90 to 0.98 in the internal cohort ( p = 0.038). In the external cohort, the mean reader AUC increased from 0.84 to 0.95, although this difference did not reach statistical significance ( p = 0.11). AI assistance also significantly reduced interobserver variability (Fleiss’s κ: 0.72 to 0.93 internally; 0.62 to 0.85 externally; both, p < 0.001). AI-based mitotic quantification provides an objective and standardized adjunct to histological grading and reduces interobserver variability. This approach may improve diagnostic accuracy and support clinical decision-making, pending prospective validation.

items.title: Deployment ergonomics, visibility-control coupling, and the assistance paradox: Findings from usability analysis of occupational exoskeletons during pre- and post-use tasks
items.abstract: Occupational exoskeletons promise significant reductions in worker physical burden and injury risk, yet industrial adoption rates remain low despite positive laboratory performance data. This persistent gap between demonstrated efficacy and actual deployment suggests that unmeasured barriers beyond task-performance metrics may influence adoption decisions. We examined whether pre- and post-use tasks generate usability problems that could act as barriers to adoption. Seven evaluators trained in human factors and heuristic evaluation evalauted three passive exoskeletons representing different support mechanisms: a shoulder-support device (Skelex), a lumbar-support device (Laevo), and a sit-stand support device (Chairless Chair). Using a combined framework of Nielsen usability heuristics and Shneiderman principles adapted for physical wearable systems, evaluators independently identified usability problems across all four deployment task phases, rated problem severity on a 5-point scale, and participated in structured reconciliation discussions to resolve rating divergences. Evaluators identified 158 usability problems across the three devices, 62 of which were rated as major problems (mean severity at or above 2.5): 29 for the shoulder-support, 15 for the back-support, and 18 for the sit-stand exoskeleton. Assembly accounted for 46% of the heuristic violations associated with major problems (114 of 250), ranging from 41% to 54% across devices. Agreement among the independent severity ratings was moderate for the seven-evaluator mean (ICC(2,7) = 0.67). Because the study did not measure adoption, these problems are plausible barriers to adoption that warrant field investigation. Six problem categories recurred across devices regardless of support mechanism, four of them in all three devices: two-person operation requirements (severity 2.9-3.1), poor documentation (severity 3.0), absent sequence indicators (severity 2.6-2.9), manual strength barriers (severity 2.7-3.1), universal design violations (severity 2.6–3.4), and hazards and safety problems, which included component ricochet on the shoulder-support device (severity 3.3–3.4), fall risk on the sit-stand device (severity 2.6–2.7), and pinch points on both. Based on our findings, we introduce three theoretical constructs extending heuristic evaluation theory to physical wearable systems: Deployment Ergonomics (encompassing physical, cognitive, temporal, and social demands of device preparation and removal), Visibility-Control Coupling (a design pattern where high force application and visual access requirements conflict), and the Assistance Paradox (the systemic contradiction whereby devices designed to reduce worker burden inadvertently create new demands, hazards, and barriers during setup). These constructs, derived from expert inspection and not yet validated in the field, offer a diagnostic framework for recurring design issues and a basis for design proposals.

items.title: Design and formative usability evaluation of a prototype integrated digital health platform for chronic care support
items.abstract: Introduction Chronic care management platforms often support only one or two core pillars of care, such as patient monitoring, patient activation, and data-driven care coordination. This fragmentation can limit the continuity of support and reduce the usefulness of shared patient data among patients, coaches, and clinicians. Method This study describes the design, software architecture, and formative usability evaluation of the Digital Health Navigator (DiNa) platform, an integrated system designed to bring together the core pillars of chronic care management. DiNa combines wearable and self-reported monitoring, a large language model-powered embodied conversational agent, and a coordinator dashboard within a single modular ecosystem. DiNa was implemented as an Android application, a web-based coordinator dashboard, a microservices backend, and wearable integrations with a smartwatch and a continuous glucose monitor. The embodied conversational agent supports goal setting, logging, reminders, and knowledge-grounded education through coaching informed by motivational interviewing and cognitive behavioural therapy. We conducted moderated laboratory think-aloud usability sessions with 10 relatively young healthy volunteers familiar with digital health tracking. Participants explored the application and completed structured tasks, including setting goals, logging meals with an image, reviewing history, interacting with the coach, and viewing trends. Results Outcomes included task performance, the System Usability Scale (SUS), a brief NASA Task Load Index (NASA-TLX), three acceptability items, and a reflexive thematic analysis of interviews. Participants completed the core tasks in a facilitated session, and a small number of critical breakdowns were observed and quantified. Mean SUS was 76.1 (SD 15.0), indicating generally good usability. Overall, the NASA-TLX workload averaged 26.7, with mental demand and effort higher than the other subscales and the remaining subscales low. Acceptability ratings indicated moderate early acceptability, with perceived usefulness rated more positively than near-term use or recommendation. Qualitative analysis identified five themes, including burdensome and sometimes unclear logging workflows, uneven goal setting, a friendly but occasionally generic coach, interface elements that reduced confidence, and a strong interest in integration with existing devices and applications. Discussion These findings provide early evidence that an integrated platform combining continuous sensing, conversational coaching, and clinician-facing coordination is technically feasible and usable in a controlled setting with healthy volunteers, and they identify the workflow refinements needed before evaluation in clinically representative populations.

items.title: Design and Implementation of an AI-Driven Business ERP System for Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises
items.abstract: This project presents the design and development of an AI-driven Business Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system intended to support small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). The system aims to integrate essential business operations into a unified platform, including inventory management, billing, customer relationship management, employee management, and sales analytics. The proposed architecture combines web-based technologies, database management, and artificial intelligence capabilities to improve business workflow integration and support data-driven decision-making. Depending on the implemented modules, AI-based features may assist with sales forecasting, business insights, and conversational business support. The project focuses on modular system design, operational efficiency, centralized data management, and usability for small businesses. Its effectiveness should be evaluated using implementation tests, functional validation, and appropriate performance measurements. This record documents the project concept, system architecture, implementation, and associated research materials.

items.title: Design of AI-Supported Scenario-Based Learning Activities for Teacher Education in the Context of Sustainable Development
items.abstract: This chapter examines how artificial intelligence (AI)-supported scenario-based learning approaches can be utilised in teacher education to develop sustainable development-oriented thinking, ethical reasoning, and systems thinking competences for decision-making. Within the framework of Education for Sustainable Development (ESD), it is critically important for pre-service teachers to understand the interrelationships among environmental, social, and economic dimensions and to develop holistic solutions tof complex problems. In this context, the chapter discusses how AI tools (specifically ChatGPT) can serve as a “learning partner” in data analysis, scenario generation, simulation, and reflective thinking. Two exemplary learning activities aligned with the SDGs are presented, modelling pre-service teachers’ decision-making processes concerning multidimensional problems such as sustainable school design, community-based environmental issues, and social justice. It is anticipated that the developed activities will enhance pre-service teachers’ data-driven thinking skills, enable them to compare the impacts of different scenarios, and support ethical evaluations. The study advocates that AI should be positioned not as an independent decision-maker but as a decision-support tool that encourages critical thinking, enhances pedagogical creativity, and strengthens sustainability awareness. In conclusion, AI-supported scenario-based teacher education offers an innovative pedagogical model that prepares future educators to be equipped both technologically and ethically, capable of guiding sustainable development.

items.abstract: This chapter provides an overview of common frameworks and approaches used for instructional design on AI as well as tangible examples and sample pedagogical activities, specifically on AI ethics, using the multiliteracies framework through a sociotechnical lens. By combining academic literacy, multimodal learning, and sociotechnical inquiry, the activities shared in the chapter can help to prepare students to become reflective, responsible, and ethically engaged participants in an increasingly AI-mediated world. It ends with a discussion of how to adapt these activities for various contexts (e.g., lower-level students, diverse student backgrounds, and different institutional policies and expectations). This chapter contributes to the field by translating broad discussions of AI ethics into structured and adaptable pedagogical applications grounded in Multiliteracies.

items.title: Developing A Human Resource Risk Management Model For Sustainable Sea Export Operations: A Design-Based Research Study In Indonesian Freight Forwarding Companies
items.abstract: Sea export operations depend heavily on human resources because freight forwarding personnel coordinate documentation, customs procedures, container handling, shipping schedules, and communication among stakeholders. Human-related failures may result in documentation errors, shipment delays, additional costs, regulatory penalties, and service disruptions. However, limited research has developed an implementable human resource risk management model specifically for freight forwarding operations. This study aims to develop a Human Resource Risk Management Model for sea export operations by integrating human factors, Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA), risk registers, mitigation procedures, competency development, and monitoring. A Design-Based Research approach was employed through problem identification, risk analysis, model design, validation, limited implementation, and evaluation at PT Ritra Logistik Semarang, Indonesia. Data were collected through observation, interviews, document analysis, focus group discussion, and practitioner validation. FMEA was used to assess and prioritize human-related failure modes. The findings identified critical risks related to export documentation, data accuracy, communication, container handling, manifest submission, competency, and procedural compliance. The study developed MARISLOG (Management of Human Resource Risk in Logistics), integrating risk identification, FMEA, risk prioritization, Risk Register, mitigation SOPs, competency-based training, monitoring, and evaluation. The model provides an implementation-oriented approach to improving operational reliability and supporting sustainable sea export operations.

items.title: Developing a Risk-Based Intellectual Property Governance Framework for Generative Artificial Intelligence: A Comparative Analysis of the Eu Ai Act, Uk, and Us Legal Systems
items.abstract: This paper develops a risk-based intellectual property (IP) governance framework for generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) through doctrinal, comparative, and normative analysis of the European Union (EU), the United Kingdom (UK), and the United States (US). It covers copyright and related IP challenges in data acquisition, model training, output creation, and commercial deployment, as well as the distribution of control, transparency, attribution, and liability in each jurisdiction. The analysis reveals that the EU has several text-and-data-mining exceptions and copyright-policy and training-content-summary obligations for general-purpose AI providers, while the UK has a very limited non-commercial research exception and a unique statutory exception for computer-generated works, and the US is driven primarily by the human-authorship doctrine and fact-specific fair-use analysis. While these strategies offer valuable protections, none alone establish a comprehensive system of organisational control. The study thus suggests an auditing framework linked to the legal basis, data provenance, licenses, human contribution to creativity, output testing, documentation, accountability and escalation, and periodic reassessment, according to the proportionate degree of risk. Rather than harmonizing the three legal systems, the framework sets out a common organizational process for identifying and managing differences in the three legal systems to safeguard the rights holders and to allow for responsible innovation.

items.title: Development and Validation of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-Generated Visual Clinic for Supplementing Clinical Teaching in Resource-Limited Settings: A Proof of Concept Study
items.abstract: Background: Clinical teaching integrates theoretical knowledge with direct patient contact. However, in resource-limited settings, adequate patient contact is often compromised by inadequate clinical facilities, perennial industrial actions by healthcare workers, and limited access to rare or under-referred cases. The aim of this study was to develop an AI-generated visual clinic (a curated catalogue of videos) depicting motor rehabilitation in patients with stroke to help supplement real-world clinical teaching. Methods: An AI platform, Topmediai (https://www.topmediai.com/app/text-to-video/) was used to generate videos on constraint-induced movement therapy (CIMT), motor imagery, sit-to-stand, over-ground gait training and treadmill gait training. The videos were edited and combined into an AI-generated visual clinic using CapCut (https://www.capcut.com/). Students and teachers were asked to rate the AI-generated visual clinic for: 1) Anatomical plausibility, 2) Procedural fidelity, 3) Rehabilitation accuracy, 4) Pedagogical clarity, and 5) Risk of learner misconception on a-5-point Likert scale, where, 1=low, 2= fair, 3=moderate, 4=high, and 5=very high. Results: A complete visual clinic demonstrating CIMT, motor imagery, sit-to-stand, over-ground gait training and treadmill gait training was produced. In addition, majority of the participants (both teachers and students), rated anatomical plausibility, procedural fidelity, rehabilitation accuracy and pedagogical clarity of the AI-generated visual clinic as high or very high; and risk of learner misconception as low or fair. Conclusion: It seems possible to generate clinically relevant videos of disease management using current AI text-to-video tools that can be catalogued into a “visual clinic” and used to support traditional clinical teaching.

items.title: Diagnosing the Explicit-to-Applied Theory of Mind Gap in LLMs
items.abstract: As large language models are deployed in high-stakes roles such as therapy, education, and personal assistance, their social cognition must be assessed reliably. Current Theory of Mind (ToM) benchmarks report aggregate scores that conflate two distinct competencies: explicit ToM (recognizing what someone believes) and applied ToM (using that belief to predict behavior). Building on this distinction, we investigate the gap and its recoverability using four structurally diverse benchmarks. Aggregate reporting obscures uneven competence: on SimpleToM, Llama-3.1-8B scores 51.5 percent overall while recognizing mental states at 99.4 percent and predicting behavior at only 28.9 percent. To assess recovery, we compare structured prompting, matched in-context learning, and our proposed Belief-State Test-Time Training (BSTTT), which adapts lightweight parameters on answered support questions through action reconstruction. Across Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, and GPT-oss-20B, recovery depends on the model, task, and intervention. On SimpleToM, reminders combined with BSTTT improve Llama's behavior prediction by 40.8 percentage points; reminders account for most of the overall improvement, with BSTTT adding 1.3 to 5.5 points beyond reminders across models. Contextual examples often outperform weight updates, while BSTTT remains stronger in specific model-benchmark settings. Temporal belief tracking remains difficult despite partial recovery. These findings show that aggregate ToM scores can overstate applied competence while hiding performance recoverable through targeted assistance. We recommend decomposed reporting of explicit and applied accuracy alongside intervention comparisons that establish which failures are recoverable and under what conditions.

items.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Artificial Intelligence versus Clinical Diagnosis in Detecting Acute Otitis Media: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
items.abstract: Abstract Acute otitis media (AOM) represents a prevalent infection in children globally, leading to considerable morbidity and imposing a substantial burden on healthcare systems. Prompt and precise diagnosis is critical to reducing complications, such as tympanic membrane perforation, hearing impairment, and excessive antibiotic prescribing. Advances in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly deep learning, have created opportunities to enhance diagnostic accuracy and broaden access to care, especially in low-resource settings. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of AI-based systems for detecting AOM compared with conventional clinical diagnosis and to analyze their accuracy relative to human clinicians across different model architectures and diagnostic methods. Following PRISMA-DTA standards and PROSPERO registration, systematic searches were conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, and IEEE Xplore up to July 30, 2025. Eligible studies included human participants with suspected AOM, employed AI-driven diagnostic approaches, and used a clinical reference standard. The Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies-2 tool assessed bias, and pooled sensitivity and specificity were estimated using a bivariate random-effects model. Nine studies published between 2020 and 2025 met the inclusion criteria. The pooled sensitivity and specificity were 91% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 77%–97%) and 99% (95% CI: 94%–100%), respectively. AI models overall matched or outperformed general practitioners and pediatricians, approaching otolaryngologist-level accuracy. AI-based tools have the potential to improve AOM detection, mitigate inequalities in healthcare access, and promote more effective diagnosis, particularly in underserved regions.

items.title: DIAL: Steerable Language Models with Distilled Instruction-Adherence Levels
items.abstract: When a user says "Keep it short", how short should the LLM's response be? More generally, users and applications require different levels of instruction adherence, but prompting does not reliably provide fine-grained control over them. We therefore study "steerable language models" that provide fine-grained numerical control over the degree to which models follow general instructions specified in text. However, existing approaches do not jointly offer fine-grained control, efficiency, and scalability across diverse instructions. To address this gap, we introduce DIAL (Distilled Instruction-Adherence Levels) to achieve all three properties. For fine-grained control, we perform classifier-free guidance (CFG) with a frozen LLM to provide training signals for on-policy distillation of instruction adherence at different levels. For efficiency, we design a lightweight steering adapter that uses a classifier over the LLM's hidden states to compute a closed-form steering edit. The classifier adaptively sets the steering magnitude at each token based on the target adherence level, while accounting for the geometry of the LLM's hidden states to preserve response coherence. For scalability, the classifier is text-conditioned, allowing a shared adapter to support new instructions without per-instruction fitting, and training requires only instruction and request text. Evaluation across multiple LLM families shows that DIAL achieves a competitive balance between concept expression and response fluency, with concept scores increasing monotonically across adherence levels. We introduce SteerIF, an instruction-only dataset of 98, 625 concept, persona, verifiable, and descriptive instructions. When trained on SteerIF, DIAL provides fine-grained control over personas and, when combined with prompting, improves verifiable instruction following.

items.title: Dialect-Aware Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Arabic Question Answering: Measuring and Mitigating the Moroccan Darija–MSA Retrieval Gap
items.abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems for Arabic are evaluated almost exclusively with Modern Standard Arabic (MSA) queries, although users write in dialect. We study this mismatch with a parallel benchmark of 200 questions written in both MSA and Moroccan Darija over 3,054 Arabic Wikipedia passages. Dialectal queries lower hybrid-retrieval Recall@1 from 0.755 to 0.620, and the loss reaches the answers: with five retrieved passages, answer correctness falls from 0.810 to 0.690, mostly through additional refusals; part of this loss persists even when the gold passage is supplied directly, so retrieval is the larger but not the only component. Rewriting Darija queries into MSA does not help. Zero-shot cross-encoder reranking raises dialectal Recall@1 to 0.800 (MSA: 0.755 unreranked, 0.875 reranked) and lets a single retrieved passage replace five unreranked passages with no loss larger than five percentage points and a 3.7-fold shorter prompt. Because dialectal queries are retrieved with lower confidence, gating the reranker on the retriever’s score margin concentrates its cost on them without any dialect detection, retaining 94% of the benefit while reranking about half of the queries. The findings hold under a human-validated LLM judge (Cohen’s κ=0.797), Holm correction and three prompt wordings, and replicate judge-free on a second, Darija-trained generator. We release the benchmark, corpus, code and all result files.

items.abstract: Differentiable Digital Twins: A Case Study in Water Distribution Presentation delivered at the 23rd International Conference on Informatics in Control, Automation and Robotics (ICINCO 2026) within the Special Session on Hybrid Artificial Intelligence (HybAI 2026) held in Angers, France, October 26–28, 2026. Summary:This presentation demonstrates a production-grade Scientific Machine Learning (SciML) framework implemented in Julia (DifferentialEquations.jl, Flux.jl) for real-time monitoring and economic dispatch in municipal water distribution networks under volatile day-ahead electricity tariffs. Technical Highlights & Contributions: Differentiable Actuator Surrogates: Replaces discontinuous relay logic with parameterized logistic sigmoid activations and first-order inertial spin-up dynamics, enabling smooth automatic differentiation through legacy SCADA thresholds. Teacher Forcing System Identification: Decouples recurrent ODE trajectory unrolling during gray-box training. Clamping states to telemetry at discrete intervals eliminates stiff numerical gradient explosions, accurately isolating unmetered pipe leakages (-2.00 L/s and -1.50 L/s) with <2.5% residual error. Multi-Phase Decoupled Training: Isolates physical actuator identification (Phase 0), neural residual training with frozen physics (Phase 1), and policy optimization with frozen twin (Phase 2). Control Barrier Function (CBF) Guarantees: Restricts policy search to discrete-time forward-invariant safe sets (margin α = 0.05), maintaining head pressure bounds unconditionally. Key Empirical Benchmarks: 38.50% Electricity Cost Reduction: Slashes total pumping expenditure from €14,369.43 (Business-as-Usual) to €8,837.68, netting €5,531.75 in savings over a 150-day continuous test horizon. Zero Safety Infractions: Exactly 0 limit violations across 150 days despite persistent pipe leaks and stochastic diurnal consumer demand. Sub-Second Online Inference: Evaluates in 12.4 ms per step—more than 11× faster than classical nonlinear MPC (145.7 ms)—eliminating online non-convex NLP solver timeouts. Open-Loop Tracking: Delivers 11.49% 72-hour open-loop NRMSE, preventing the severe divergence observed in nominal white-box physics (121.16% NRMSE). items.title: Digital and artificial intelligence-assisted medication management for older adults with chronic diseases: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
items.abstract: Objective This systematic review and meta-analysis aims to synthesize the results of randomized controlled trials to determine whether medication management approaches based on digital technologies and artificial intelligence/machine learning can indeed bring measurable clinical improvements in older adults with at least one chronic diseases. Methods To identify relevant RCTs, we performed a systematic search of PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, CNKI, Wanfang, and other databases from their inception through June 30, 2026, for studies of digital and AI/ML-based medication management in older adults with at least one chronic diseases. All stages of study selection, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment were conducted independently by two reviewers, applying the Cochrane RoB 2.0 tool. Meta-analytic pooling was conducted via RevMan 5.4. Results Nineteen RCTs met the inclusion criteria, of which 6 were included in the meta-analysis and 13 in the descriptive synthesis. For medication adherence, three studies reported highly heterogeneous results ( I 2 = 97%), and because of this heterogeneity and the small number of studies, the data were not pooled; the individual study estimates ranged from SMD = −0.28–SMD = 1.89. For PIMs, only one study reported a comparable outcome; no pooled estimate was calculated. For hospitalization and mortality, the two included studies used different effect measures (HR and OR) and were therefore presented separately: Blum et al. reported an HR of 0.95 (95% CI 0.77–1.17), and Rieckert et al. reported an OR of 0.88 (95% CI 0.73–1.07). Conclusion The current body of evidence does not establish clinically meaningful benefits of digital or AI/ML-based medication management on hard endpoints such as hospitalization and mortality among older adults with at least one chronic diseases. For medication adherence, the evidence remains inconclusive and highly heterogeneous, and no reliable pooled estimate could be obtained. Given the pronounced heterogeneity and the limited pool of high-quality RCTs, current evidence is insufficient to establish clinical benefit for the routine implementation of digital or AI/ML-based medication management systems in geriatric care and further rigorously designed studies are warranted. items.title: DIGITAL FORENSIC ACCOUNTING: INTEGRATING DIGITAL EVIDENCE, ADVANCED ANALYTICS AND PROFESSIONAL JUDGEMENT FOR FRAUD DETECTION AND FINANCIAL INTEGRITY
items.abstract: The fast growth of digital technology in financial systems has changed the nature of financial fraud. This has created new problems for traditional methods of accounting, auditing and investigation. Because of this, digital forensic accounting has become more important. It is a multidisciplinary approach that combines accounting knowledge, investigative methods, digital forensics and advanced technologies. This study examines the role of digital forensic accounting in fraud detection, financial investigation and financial integrity. It uses a conceptual and narrative review of academic literature, professional reports and reliable sources. The review shows that digital evidence, data analytics, artificial intelligence and machine learning can help identify suspicious transactions. These tools can also help examine financial data and trace financial activities. Digital forensic accounting supports fraud prevention, internal controls, transparency, accountability and corporate governance. However, technological complexity, privacy concerns, legal and ethical issues and the need for specialised skills remain important challenges.

items.abstract: Digital health and artificial intelligence are becoming influential in shaping global health policy due to the opportunities they will offer in improving access, efficiency and health outcomes globally. It examines policy issues concerning governance, regulation, and human rights and the role of international collaboration when working towards equitable and responsible adoption of health technologies using artificial intelligence.

items.title: Digital Illusions and Cognitive Crisis: Governing the Negative Externalities of Internet and AI in Education
items.abstract: The Internet and artificial intelligence (AI) have become deeply embedded in contemporary education, research and professional life. Their capacity to enhance learning efficiency and reduce access costs is undeniable. Yet these technologies have also generated significant negative externalities: students are increasingly distanced from printed textbooks and library-based study, turning instead to instantly available digital resources and generative AI tools. This shift has contributed to the erosion of deep reading, critical thinking and creativity. Drawing on recent empirical evidence, this article analyses the mechanisms through which screen-based reading and AI dependence undermine cognitive development, and argues that educational institutions must intervene through formal rules and regulations to minimise these externalities. It proposes a policy framework centred on the principle of preserving cognitive friction, encompassing curriculum design, pedagogical norms and assessment reform.

items.title: Digital Servitization in Service-Oriented Manufacturing Through Dynamic Capabilities and Supply Chain Transformation
items.abstract: This chapter examines how Industry 4.0 technologies reshape servitization and service-oriented manufacturing within digitally transforming supply chains. While digital servitization is often associated with technologies such as IoT, artificial intelligence, cloud platforms, analytics, and digital twins, the chapter argues that technology adoption alone is insufficient to generate service-oriented performance. Drawing on service-dominant logic, business model innovation, supply chain integration, socio-technical systems thinking, and dynamic capabilities theory, the chapter develops a theory-informed model explaining how manufacturers sense digital service opportunities, seize them through Industry 4.0-enabled service offerings, and reconfigure supply chain relationships around lifecycle value creation. The model is applied to an anonymous industrial equipment manufacturing case that illustrates the transition from product sales and reactive maintenance toward predictive maintenance, remote diagnostics, lifecycle service agreements, and recurring service revenue. The chapter contributes by positioning digital servitization as a capability-driven supply chain transformation and highlights practical conditions related to data governance, supplier readiness, customer trust, cybersecurity, and service-oriented performance measurement.

items.title: Digital transformation in higher scientific education: The roles of virtual simulation, AI-assisted learning, and blended teaching
items.abstract: The accelerating digitisation of higher education has prompted urgent questions about which technology-mediated pedagogical interventions most effectively improve student learning outcomes in scientific disciplines. Drawing on a cross-institutional survey of 1500 undergraduate and postgraduate students enrolled in STEM and scientific programmes across five institution types, this study investigates the individual and joint effects of three canonical digital transformation mechanisms: virtual simulation laboratories (VSL), artificial intelligence-assisted learning (AIAAL), and blended teaching models (BTM). Employing a mixed-methods empirical framework that combines structural equation modelling (SEM), multi-level fixed-effects regression, and bootstrap mediation analysis, we estimate standardised direct effects of 0.264, 0.218, and 0.192 for VSL, AIAAL, and BTM on academic achievement, respectively. Mediation analysis reveals that self-regulated learning (SRL), collaborative knowledge construction, and cognitive engagement jointly channel 55.5% of the VSL effect and 54.7% of the AIAAL effect through indirect pathways, underscoring the primacy of process-level learning mechanisms. Moderation analysis demonstrates that institutional readiness amplifies all three technology effects by 42-68%, while disciplinary context generates the sharpest differential: VSL effects in STEM disciplines are 110% larger than in non-STEM contexts, whereas AIAAL effects remain comparably robust across disciplines. Robustness tests using instrumental variables, propensity score matching, and difference-in-differences quasi-experimental designs confirm that results are not artefacts of selection bias or omitted variable contamination. Policy scenario projections to 2030 suggest that full digital integration could reduce inter-institutional achievement gaps by 74% relative to business-as-usual. The findings contribute a theoretically grounded and empirically validated framework for evidence-based digital transformation in scientific higher education.

items.title: Digital Transformation: Artificial Intelligence Adoption of Small Medium Enterprises in Gauteng
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is now a crucial element in the transforming of industries globally, propelled by greater development in computational processing, cloud and computational services, and deep learning technologies. Its uses, ranging from chatbots to self-driving cars, are becoming more widespread, presenting the opportunity to enhance organizational efficiency by as much as 40%. In light of global competitiveness and digital transformation, which have been induced by the COVID-19 era, AI is crucial, especially for Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs). Nevertheless, SMEs face considerable obstacles to AI acceptance, such as financial and technical limitations, restricted access to advanced technologies, and a shortage of skilled personnel. These issues hinder their productivity and competitiveness within the national economy. This research investigates the elements that affect AI acceptance in the landscape of SMEs in Gauteng, with the goal of identifying barriers, evaluating the impact of managerial leadership, and assessing the use of AI in operations. A sample of 118 stakeholders, including owners, managers, and strategic employees from various backgrounds, was analysed, excluding large corporations and government entities. The study focuses on the ICT sector, exploring technological, organizational, environmental, and ethical aspects of AI implementation. The capstone report aims to formulate strategies that assist SMEs in overcoming challenges related to digital transformation, offering an introduction, literature review, methodology, analysis, and strategic recommendations specifically designed for the South African context. This research demonstrates that AI adoption among Gauteng's SMEs stands at a critical inflection point. Strong awareness of AI's potential combines with substantial adoption intentions, creating conditions for rapid diffusion. However, realising this potential requires coordinated action addressing identified barriers through organisational capability building, ecosystem enablement, and supportive policy frameworks. items.title: Digital Twin-Assisted Physics-Informed Graph Neural Network Framework with Explainable Artificial Intelligence for Personalized Drug Delivery Optimization
items.abstract: The growing demand for personalized drug delivery necessitates intelligent computational approaches that can jointly analyze molecular characteristics, biological targets, physicochemical properties, and therapeutic responses.This study presents a Digital Twin-Assisted Physics-Informed Graph Neural Network (PI-GNN) integrated with Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) to facilitate drug-target response prediction and personalized therapeutic optimization.The proposed framework was developed using 52,274 drug-target interaction records, partitioned into 36,592 training, 5,227 validation, and 10,455 testing samples.Molecular structures were transformed into graphs characterized by 23 atom-level and six bond-level features, while protein sequences were represented through 24 biological attributes.Eight physicochemical parameters-molecular weight, LogP, topological polar surface area (TPSA), hydrogen-bond donors, hydrogen-bond acceptors, rotatable bonds, ring count, and fraction Csp3-were incorporated to provide physics-informed constraints to the learning process.Experimental evaluation on the log-transformed response yielded an R² of 0.4209, RMSE of 2.2985, and MAE of 1.5695 for the test dataset.Permutation-based XAI revealed TPSA as the dominant physicochemical contributor, with its perturbation increasing RMSE by 0.1662 and decreasing R² by 0.0868, followed by molecular weight, LogP, ring count, and hydrogen-bond donors.Molecular-level interpretability was further established using GNNExplainer to identify influential atoms associated with individual predictions.Input-ablation analysis showed that suppressing physicochemical and protein information reduced R² from 0.4209 to -5.0589 and 0.3276, respectively, indicating that the trained network relied substantially on these complementary information sources.The XAI-guided digital-twin module evaluated 10,661 valid molecular candidates, with 5,756 satisfying the specified drug-like constraints.For the selected biological target context, Drug ID 1049 was identified as the highest-ranked candidate, increasing the predicted log-response from 8.5935 to 15.5521, representing an 80.98% relative improvement on the modelled log-response scale and achieving a digital-twin score of 0.8905.Overall, the findings indicate that combining graph-based molecular learning with physicochemical knowledge, model explainability, and digital-twin-driven candidate screening offers an interpretable computational strategy for prioritizing promising drug-target configurations.The framework provides a foundation for subsequent experimental validation and the development of data-driven personalized drug-delivery systems.

items.title: Dilemmas and Optimization Strategies for the Professional Development of Higher Vocational College Teachers in Inner Mongolia from the Perspective of Educational Ecology
items.abstract: Background: The professional development of higher vocational college teachers is shaped not only by individual competence but also by the relationships among colleges, industry partners, policy systems, digital resources, and regional conditions. In Inner Mongolia, a useful analytical approach must account for both the common pressures of vocational education and the region’s diverse economic and geographic settings. Aim: This paper examines key dilemmas affecting teacher professional development and proposes an ecology-oriented framework for improvement. Methodology: It adopts a conceptual, literature-based analysis of the four Chinese studies supplied for this paper, supplemented by a contextual review of publicly available material on vocational education and teacher development in the region. It does not claim to report original survey or interview data. Findings: The analysis identifies five connected challenges: an insufficiently differentiated professional role, uneven access to authentic workplace learning, fragmented institutional support, a gap between digital tools and pedagogical application, and evaluation mechanisms that may privilege visible outputs over sustained growth. These challenges are interpreted through the ecological concepts of niche, interaction, limiting factors, and the “flowerpot effect.” Conclusion: Sustainable improvement requires coordinated action at teacher, college, industry, and regional-policy levels. The paper recommends differentiated development pathways, long-term school–enterprise learning communities, practice-oriented digital development, more supportive evaluation, and regionally responsive resource sharing. These proposals should be tested through empirical research in representative institutions across Inner Mongolia.

items.title: Directing to Diversify: Multi-Directional Search for Automatic Heuristic Design
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong potential to automate heuristic design for NP-hard combinatorial optimization (CO) tasks without human intervention. Recent methods predominantly rely on evolutionary computation (EC) frameworks, where heuristic diversification is mainly induced through EC-like operators or downstream selection, while the direction of heuristic transformation remains largely unharnessed. In this paper, we propose a multi-directional Perturbation-Rewrite Search (PRS) framework for automatic heuristic design that factorizes heuristic transformation through directional search primitives at the generation level. Specifically, PRS operates on heuristic ideas through three complementary directions: expansion toward richer and more expressive designs, compression toward simpler and less specialized designs, and steering for fine-grained refinement, together enabling broader and more sustained exploration of diverse regions in the heuristic design space. PRS further organizes candidate exploration within a breadth-first search-based process with adaptive operator control, which ensures thorough candidate utilization and sustained exploration, and maintains strong search dynamics while preventing premature convergence. Extensive empirical results across diverse CO tasks show that PRS consistently discovers high-quality heuristics, demonstrating the effectiveness and generality of explicitly directional exploration design.

items.title: DIRECTIVE SPEECH ACTS IN RESEARCHER–AI INTERACTION: A REFLEXIVE CASE STUDY OF ACADEMIC JOURNAL SUBMISSION
items.abstract: This study investigates the realisation and interactional functions of directive speech acts in researcher–AI communication through a reflexive case study of an academic journal submission. While directive speech acts have been extensively examined in human–human institutional interactions, limited empirical attention has been paid to how directives are constructed and deployed when the addressee is an artificial intelligence (AI) system operating within digitally mediated academic workflows. As AI systems increasingly assist scholars in writing and navigating editorial platforms, it is necessary to examine how action, authority, and epistemic responsibility are negotiated in human–AI interactions. This study addresses this gap by analysing a naturally occurring dialogue between a researcher and ChatGPT during the real-time submission of a manuscript to an international Q1 journal. The dataset comprised a complete 46-turn interaction sequence, from which 16 researcher-initiated directive moves were identified as primary units of analysis. Adopting a qualitative reflexive case study design, the analysis draws on speech act theory (Searle, 1976), interactional epistemics (Heritage, 2012), and relational work (Locher & Watts, 2008) to examine the linguistic realisation and functional deployment of directives across submission stages. The findings reveal that directives are predominantly realised through interrogative constructions rather than bald imperatives. WH-questions (e.g., “What should I do?”) and yes/no interrogatives pragmatically function as action-eliciting moves, particularly at moments of procedural uncertainty. These interrogatives enable the researcher to seek guidance while mitigating imposition, constructing AI as a procedural authority without an overt command. In addition to interrogatives, mitigated imperatives (e.g. “please explain”) and declarative problem reports (e.g., “I clicked OK, but there is no response”) operate as directive resources, demonstrating that directive force is interactionally achieved rather than strictly encoded in the grammatical mood. Functionally, four directive categories emerged: procedural guidance, explanatory mediation, confirmation for epistemic risk management, and evaluative positioning. Procedural guidance directives are clustered during technically opaque stages, such as PDF generation and final approval. Explanatory directives seek clarification of institutional prompts, positioning AI as an interpretive mediator. Confirmation directives appear before irreversible actions, reflecting heightened epistemic caution. A smaller subset of evaluative directives solicits normative stances regarding open-access decisions, extending human–AI interaction into moral reasoning. Directive density increases in phases characterised by institutional opacity, suggesting a correlation between procedural risks and directive production. Notably, directives are consistently mitigated through relational address terms and politeness markers despite the AI’s nonhuman status. This persistence of mitigation indicates that relational framing may function as a routinised communicative schema rather than solely as a face-protecting adjustment. Overall, this study argues that directives in researcher–AI interactions operate as mechanisms of institutional navigation and epistemic regulation rather than coercive command structures, contributing to empirical insights into the emerging field of human–AI pragmatics.

items.title: DISC: Domain-Integrated Similarity Cost for Time-Series Dataset
items.abstract: The growth of time-series datasets and foundation models has made dataset comparison a central part of time-series workflows. Assessing source-target transfer before model adaptation requires similarity estimates that can summarize transfer-related dataset relationships without exhaustive source-target evaluation over every candidate pair. Many metrics have been proposed for measuring similarity between time-series datasets, but they capture different dataset relationships and vary in how well they align with downstream utility across tasks. We evaluate this gap by measuring the correlation between source-target similarity scores and downstream forecasting errors in out-of-distribution and transfer-learning settings. We propose Domain-Integrated Similarity Cost (DISC), a learnable aggregation framework that uses calibration transfer observations to select, weight, and combine similarity metrics for different downstream tasks. By integrating complementary metric values, DISC better distinguishes source-target dataset differences that matter for downstream behavior. After calibration, DISC scores source-target pairs using only their similarity-metric values and yields higher alignment than single-metric references on the reported split. These results show that time-series dataset similarity is task-dependent, and that learned metric integration provides a stronger proxy for downstream transfer behavior than manually selecting one similarity metric.

items.title: Does Managing Religious Diversity Enhance Employee Engagement and Retention in Hotels? The Moderating Role of Ethical Leadership
items.abstract: Respect for religious diversity creates a welcoming hotel environment, benefiting guests, staff, and the business’s overall performance. Anchored in the theory of planned behavior (TPB), this study examines the relationships between implementation of religious diversity management practices (RDMPs), employee engagement, staff intention to continue working in a hotel, and the moderating role of ethical leadership. This research employs a quantitative design, gathering data through a survey of 522 employees in the Egyptian hotel sector. The results indicate that RDMPs exert a beneficial impact on both employee engagement and the intention to remain. Ethical leadership also acts as a moderator on the relationships between RDMPs and physical engagement, RDMPs and emotional engagement, and RDMPs and cognitive engagement. Hoteliers should provide training that demonstrate the importance of RDMPs to managers and staff. Recognition of employees’ religious beliefs can include considering nutritional requirements and religious holidays. Leaders who model ethical behavior can have a significant impact on how RDMPs are implemented, aiding in the development of a work culture of mutual respect and trust. The research provides new directions in studying the management of religious diversity, particularly in the Global South and Muslim-majority countries.

items.title: Domain adaptation state of health estimation for lithium-ion batteries accounting for state of charge dependence
items.abstract: Accurate State of Health (SOH) estimation is essential for ensuring the safety, reliability, and long-term performance of electric vehicle batteries. However, the generalization performance of Artificial Intelligence methods depends on the quality and coverage of training data. Acquiring high-quality labeled data with sufficient coverage remains a challenge. To address this, this paper first comprehensively compares and analyzes the State of Charge (SOC) dependence of the mechanical, electrical, and thermal features of batteries under different initial SOC. Features with weak SOC dependence are selected as model inputs, enabling robust SOH estimation in partial charge–discharge scenarios using only fully completed charge–discharge data. This effectively reduces the model’s demand for broad data coverage. Then, this paper proposes a domain adaptation method based on Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD), which integrates the Transformer and Kolmogorov–Arnold Network (KAN). Experimental results show that adopting features with weak SOC dependence reduces the relative Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) by 85.48% for slow charging and 64.33% for fast charging. Moreover, the proposed domain adaptation method achieves a 47.69% relative reduction in MAPE.

items.title: Dual effects of AI on academic work performance: A job demands-resources theory systematic review
items.abstract: Background Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly reshaping academic work, yet its occupational health implications for academicians remain under-examined. The Job Demands-Resources (JD-R) framework offers a dual lens for understanding AI as both a performance-enhancing resource and a source of job demands, but no systematic review has applied this framework across the full spectrum of academic roles. Objective This systematic review examines how AI impacts academicians’ performance across four core domains—teaching, research, community engagement, and professional development—using the JD-R framework to understand AI's dual nature as both a resource and a demand. Methods Following PRISMA guidelines and the five-stage framework of Khan et al., 1 we systematically searched Scopus and Web of Science databases for empirical studies published between 2021 and 2025. After screening 868 records, 30 peer-reviewed journal articles met the inclusion criteria. A two-phase coding approach (deductive and inductive) was employed, with intercoder reliability (Cohen's Kappa = 0.91) indicating strong agreement. Thematic analysis was guided by the JD-R framework. Results Teaching performance dominates the literature (70%), reflecting AI's immediate impact on instructional practices. AI functions as a job resource through enhanced personalized learning, assessment automation, and administrative efficiency when supported by self-efficacy, AI literacy, and institutional resources. However, AI creates significant job demands including academic integrity management, assessment redesign, continuous upskilling, and ethical dilemmas. Professional development (27%) exhibits the most severe demand-resource imbalance, with faculty experiencing skill obsolescence anxiety, technostress, and imposter syndrome. Research performance (20%) shows a relatively balanced profile, while community engagement (7%) remains critically understudied. Identity-threatening demands—academic integrity in teaching, authorship ambiguity in research, and skill obsolescence in professional development—generate disproportionate psychological strain requiring specialized buffers. Conclusions AI's impact on academic work is inherently dualistic, with outcomes determined by the balance between available resources and demand intensity. Psychological resources, particularly self-efficacy, emerge as the most powerful enablers mediating the effectiveness of institutional and knowledge resources. The review extends JD-R theory by identifying identity-threatening demands as a distinct demand category and proposing a Resource Cascade Model wherein distal organizational resources foster proximal psychological resources. Institutions must adopt systemic, autonomy-supportive interventions addressing the full spectrum of AI's impact on academic work.

items.abstract: The article substantiates the structure, assessment criteria and levels of managerial competence of preschool leaders in dual in-service training. Effective leadership practices in early childhood education, personal leadership resources and theories of workplace learning were comparatively analysed. Competence was interpreted as a two-dimensional construct formed at the intersection of four practice domains and four personal resources, and criteria and indicators were defined for each domain. A four-level scale based on the Dreyfus model and a development cycle linking the training institution with the preschool organisation were proposed.

items.title: Early Stroke and Panic Detection using AI in Neurology
items.abstract: Neurological emergencies span a wide spectrum, from sudden vascular events such as ischemic stroke to acute psychiatric-neurological crises such as panic attacks. Both categories are time-sensitive and both currently rely heavily on manual clinical assessment, which limits the speed and consistency of detection. This paper presents a detailed review of six recent peer-reviewed sources (2024–2025) on artificial intelligence (AI) in neurology, and uses their combined findings to build a case for, and a design of, an integrated two-module early-detection framework: an imaging-based deep-learning pipeline for stroke triage, and a wearable-sensor-based sequence-modelling pipeline for panic/anxiety detection. The review covers foundational AI concepts (machine learning, deep learning, neural network architectures), the current clinical evidence base for stroke-imaging AI, the comparatively nascent evidence for physiological/behavioural AI in affective and psychiatric-neurological states, and the shared ethical, technical, and regulatory challenges — interpretability, bias, data privacy, and validation — that recur across every source reviewed. The paper then details a proposed system architecture, dataset and preprocessing requirements, candidate model architectures, an evaluation plan with specific metrics, expected outcomes, and a discussion of limitations and future work. The overall conclusion is that stroke-detection AI is a mature and clinically validated field that can serve as a design template for a still-emerging class of wearable, sensor-driven AI tools for detecting acute panic and anxiety states.

items.abstract: Issue No. 69 of Rhetoric and Communications continues the tradition of publishing research findings obtained through both traditional and contemporary methods, focusing on new and rapidly evolving fields of analysis, such as artificial intelligence, digitalization, the media ecosystem, and changes in education at the university and school levels. This issue brings together 12 scholarly articles in two sections. The first one is titled “Communication in Media and Society”, and two of the articles in this section are devoted to fact-checking, a topical issue in contemporary media and communication studies. In one article, researchers Milen Filipov and Nilufar Sulaimonova present findings related to an analysis of fact-checking activities in the media in Kazakhstan. In the second article, Tihomira Doncheva presents the results of a study on fact-checking and the use of artificial intelligence. The second area of research focuses on the media in Bulgaria. Aneta Milkova examines the legal framework, the limits of media regulation, and communication. Tanya Dimova discusses the functions of the Bulgarian National Radio, emphasizing the cultural role of the “Hristo Botev” program while taking into account changes in the digital media landscape. Alexander Blagoev presents the results of a study on social identity in communication through memes and participation in online challenges. Damyan Bumbalov clarifies, from a theoretical and methodological perspective, the scope and content of the concept of “monumental sculpture” and its communicative functions in public space. The second section includes interesting publications in which rhetoric and communication are studied in university and school settings. Faculty members from two universities in Ukraine – Mykola Chursin, Halyna Shevchenko, Tetiana Antonenko, and Tetiana Zinovieva – present the results of a timely and in-depth theoretical review related to changes in higher education resulting from technological transformations and the rapid integration of artificial intelligence into the educational process. The topic of artificial intelligence is also addressed in several other articles. Radeya Gesheva analyzes the transformations in the didactics of foreign-language literature in the era of artificial intelligence, focusing on Italian literature, for the teaching of which she provides many excellent practical examples in terms of methodology. Rhetoric is explored in new and interesting fields from a scholarly and methodological perspective: art, theater, education, and teaching in academic and school settings. Evgenia Roeva presents the findings of a study on the application of rhetoric and public speaking in education and its intersections with educational theater when working with elementary school students. Ralitsa Bezhan presents the results of a study on fundamental rhetorical canons from Aristotle to the era of artificial intelligence, contemporary theatrical performances and productions, and chatbots. Irena Shunina presents, in a captivating and compelling manner, the rhetoric of the heart and ethics in Shalva Amonashvili’s humanistic pedagogy. items.title: Education in the era of artificial intelligence from a cross-border perspective regarding student perceptions, meta-competences and institutional integration
items.abstract: Purpose The accelerated transformations of the digital economy require a profound rethinking of higher education, especially in terms of preparing human capital for a future shaped by artificial intelligence (AI). The use of AI is no longer a peripheral technological option. Still, it has become a central vector in defining the skills required in the labour market, streamlining educational processes, and reshaping the relationship between learning and performance. Design/methodology/approach This paper aims to analyse, from a cross-border perspective, how AI is integrated into higher education in Romania, the Republic of Moldova and Ukraine. The investigation examines the relationships among available educational resources, AI use, AI-related skills, meta-competencies, self-reported perceived academic performance and career intentions in an emerging digital context. Findings The study uses a convergent mixed-methods design, combining survey data from 678 students with 76 semi-structured interviews with university teachers. The findings show that AI adoption is shaped by the interaction between institutional resources, actual use, AI-related skills, meta-competencies and national context. Students from Romania and the Republic of Moldova reported more frequent and varied AI use than students from Ukraine, while the Ukrainian profile reflected a more cautious pattern shaped by risk perception and contextual constraints. The results also indicate that resources and institutional support matter mainly when they translate into concrete AI use and competence development. Originality/value The study contributes empirically and contextually to comparative research on educational technology adoption by showing that AI integration in higher education depends not only on technological acceptance, but also on institutional readiness, educational equity, digital access and responsible pedagogical governance.

items.title: Educational Innovation In Health: Impact Of Digital Technologies On Clinical Training
items.abstract: The rapid advancement of digital technologies has transformed health sciences education, particularly in the field of clinical training.This systematic review aimed to analyze the impact of digital technologies on clinical training in health sciences education.The review was conducted following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines.A comprehensive literature search was performed in three major databases: Scopus, PubMed/MEDLINE, and Web of Science.The search initially identified 498 records.After removing duplicates and applying eligibility criteria, 18 studies were included in the qualitative synthesis.The included studies examined various digital technologies applied to clinical education, including simulation-based learning systems, artificial intelligence tools, digital learning platforms, and online educational resources.Overall, the findings indicate that digital technologies significantly enhance clinical training by improving procedural skills, clinical reasoning, and student engagement.Simulation environments and virtual learning systems provide safe and controlled settings where students can practice clinical procedures without compromising patient safety.Additionally, digital educational platforms facilitate flexible learning and promote the development of digital competencies among healthcare students and professionals.Despite these benefits, challenges such as technological infrastructure limitations and the need for faculty training remain important considerations.In conclusion, digital technologies represent a valuable strategy for strengthening clinical education and preparing healthcare professionals for increasingly technology-driven healthcare systems.

items.abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis aims to evaluate the effectiveness of artificial intelligence-based therapeutic conversational agent interventions for depressive and anxiety symptoms among university students. The review focuses on parallel-group randomized controlled trials evaluating therapeutic conversational agents or chatbots designed to provide psychological treatment or therapeutic psychological support. The primary outcomes are depressive and anxiety symptoms measured using validated assessment instruments.

items.title: Effects of Digital Tools on Design Cognition in the Conceptual Phase
items.abstract: The rapid development of digital technology has significantly influenced the entire design process, particularly the conceptual phase, affecting designers’ cognition and creativity. This study systematically reviewed the literature to provide a comprehensive understanding of how digital tools support design cognition in the conceptual design phase and identify future research directions. The findings indicate that individual digital tools offer various advantages, such as providing broader perspectives, facilitating rapid idea development, and enhancing motivation. However, the strength and generalizability of the evidence were constrained by limitations in participant sampling and variation in reliability and validity procedures across studies. The review identified key areas for future research, including exploring the cognitive benefits of artificial intelligence (AI) design tools with designers, applying innovative methods and analyses to understand design cognition, examining the benefits of digital tools in simulated professional design environments, and exploring distributed collaborative design settings. The study highlighted the need for further research to deepen understanding of digital tools and their application in conceptual design.

items.title: Effects of question-chain prompting on self-regulated learning, metacognition, and achievement in a generative AI environment
items.abstract: Abstract Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) offers learners immediate and personalized support, yet unguided interaction may encourage passive use and weaken self-regulated learning (SRL). This study examined whether question-chain prompting can support SRL in human-AI interaction. A quasi-experiment was conducted with 83 undergraduates enrolled in a television program production course. A control group used free-form questioning, whereas two experimental groups used either a progressive or a divergent question-chain strategy. Data included GenAI interaction logs, post-task reflections, metacognitive awareness measures, and course grades. This study found that both question-chain groups demonstrated significantly more learning-strategy and learning-monitoring behaviors than the control group. Reflection data further indicated differences in students’ approaches to human-AI collaboration, although these differences should be interpreted cautiously because the reflection prompts differed by condition. Moreover, both experimental groups scored significantly higher than the control group on knowledge of cognition, regulation of cognition, and academic achievement. No significant differences were found between the progressive and divergent question-chain approaches. The findings suggest that question-chain prompting, implemented as an instructional package of specific, sequenced, and required questions, can promote more active engagement during human-AI interaction and support metacognitive development and learning performance. Question chains offer a practical approach for guiding students’ use of GenAI in educational settings.

items.title: El modelo pedagógico de innovación crítica: metodología para el fortalecimiento del conocimiento y el aprendizaje en los estudiantes de pregrado
items.abstract: Background. Pedagogical innovation is one of the main challenges facing higher education in the twenty-first century, as digital transformation now shapes every mode of instruction and calls into question the way students build knowledge. Objective. To develop an emerging pedagogical model that strengthens knowledge and learning among undergraduate students, drawing on the experiences of students, faculty, and administrators across different educational modes. Methods. A qualitative study was conducted under the interpretive-critical paradigm using a grounded theory design. A total of 221 participants from three Colombian institutions representing on-campus, military on-campus, and online modes were selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, supported by document analysis of reports issued by the Colombian Ministry of National Education and by observational research. The analysis involved open, axial, and selective coding, source triangulation, and categorical convergence analysis. Results. Eight emerging categories were identified: pedagogical innovation as the organizing axis, participation and dialogue, reflective assessment, critical thinking, faculty development, educational equity, meaningful learning, and the pedagogical use of artificial intelligence and ICT. The three groups agreed that changing educational practice depends not on adopting technology or making isolated methodological changes, but on aligning pedagogy, didactics, teaching strategies, and the instructional context. Conclusions. The convergence of these categories gives rise to the Pedagogical Model of Critical Innovation, an emerging theoretical construct that offers a conceptual reference for updating institutional education projects, pedagogical models, and curriculum designs across the different modes of higher education.

items.title: Electorates' Responses to AI-Generated and Human-Created Campaign Messages in South-South Nigeria Ahead of the 2027 General Elections: An Exploratory Qualitative Study
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is reshaping how political campaigns are produced and circulated. In Nigeria, parties, candidates, and supporters now rely heavily on digital tools to create adverts, images, and voice messages, yet little is known about how ordinary electorates in South-South Nigeria read such content. This exploratory study therefore examined how registered voters in South-South Nigeria distinguish AI-generated from human-created campaign messages, explain their trust or distrust in them, and describe their emotional responses and possible voting intentions ahead of the 2027 elections. A qualitative exploratory design was used. Nineteen registered voters aged 18–40 who actively use social media were purposively selected for maximum variation. Data were collected through online semi-structured interviews using six campaign messages, along with observation notes, and analysed with reflexive thematic analysis. Participants identified AI mainly through unnatural movement, implausible settings and contextual inconsistencies. Human-created messages were generally trusted more, although emotionally relevant AI content could also appear credible. Emotional reactions included humour, hope, confusion and worry, but these rarely translated directly into voting intention. Within this sample, recognition, trust and voting responses depended on realism, relevance, prior knowledge and candidate credibility. As exploratory findings, these are not statistically generalisable but offer propositions for larger, representative studies.
